**(p-140) Surah Luqman, upon him be peace**

Its purpose is to establish that the Book has wisdom, which is necessary because its Revealer, may He be glorified, is wise in His words and deeds. The story of Luqman, after whom the surah is named, is a clear proof of this. It is as if He, glorified is He, when He had completed what He intended from the beginning of the Qur'an to the end of Bara'ah (Surah al-Tawbah), which is the surah of the Byzantine campaign (Surah al-Rum), and had begun the Qur'an [after Umm al-Qur'an (al-Fatihah)] by negating doubt about this Book and affirming that it is guidance for the God-fearing, and had provided evidence for this in the surahs that followed, then began Surah Yunus after Surah al-Rum with the establishment of its wisdom. He followed that with its proof until He concluded Surah al-Rum. He began a new cycle in a more magnificent manner than the first. So He described it at the beginning of this surah that follows al-Rum with what He had described it with in Yunus, which follows the campaign against the Byzantines. That description is wisdom. He added that it is guidance and a source of guidance for the muhsinun (those who do good). These are the people of the ends, and the muttaqun (God-fearing) are the people of the beginnings.

When He established in Al 'Imran that it was sent down with the truth, He established in al-Sajdah its descent and negated doubt that it is from Him, and He established that it is the Truth. He continued after this in the surahs that follow, mostly corresponding to what came before, as is known by careful reflection, contemplation and pondering:

"In the name of Allah" (Bismillah), who encompassed everything with mercy and knowledge.

(p-141) "The Most Merciful" (al-Rahman), who scattered, through the generality of His wisdom, the comprehensive scope of His blessing across all His creation.

"The Most Compassionate" (al-Rahim), who illuminated for His elect the path to His Garden, so they persist and are bewildered in His love.

When al-Rum was concluded with the exhortation to knowledge, which is what this great Book contains, and with the command to be patient and hold fast to what it contains of promise, and with the prohibition of hoping for the people of frivolity to draw near to them in any of the attributes, and that was the wisdom, He began the first of this surah with: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim﴾, indicating that Allah, the Sovereign, the Most High, the Self-Subsisting, sent, because He is the Manifest although He is the Hidden, Jibril (Gabriel), upon him be peace, to Muhammad (ﷺ), upon him be peace, with a clear revelation of wisdoms and rulings, with what no Imam before him had articulated, and no one will reach in that matter for all time. He is the beginning and He is the seal. To this his expression with the particle of distance indicates in His saying: ﴿Those﴾, that is, the verses which are of such height and greatness that none attains them except one who strives against his own self until he refines it by renouncing all vices and adorning it with all virtues, ﴿are the verses of the Book﴾ that comprises all kinds of good, ﴿the Wise﴾, by placing things in the most fitting of their ranks, so that no part of its firm decree can be undone and no part of its speech can be opposed. This indicates the perfection of the knowledge of its Revealer and His expertise, the comprehensiveness of His greatness and power, and the subtlety of His craftsmanship in its marvelous wisdom (p-142). Therefore there is no escape from the victory of the believers and those close to them in holding fast to a Book that has a source from Allah.

Imam Abu Ja'far Ibn al-Zubayr said: When the command to take heed, the urging toward it, and the alerting to the wonders of creation were repeated in Surah al-Rum, such as His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Do they not reflect within themselves? Allah did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth﴾ [al-Rum: 8], and His saying: ﴿Have they not traveled through the earth?﴾ [al-Rum: 9], and His saying: ﴿Allah originates creation, then repeats it﴾ [al-Rum: 11], and His saying: ﴿He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living﴾ [al-Rum: 19], up to His saying: ﴿Thus do We detail the verses for a people who reason﴾ [al-Rum: 28]. These are ten verses that carried such sublime taking of heed and alerting that no doubt or hesitation remains for one who is granted success to what follows them of verses of alerting, expounding proofs, mentioning the nature upon which the servants were created, and striking parables that clarify the straight path for one who understands their meanings and reflects on their wisdoms, up to His saying: ﴿And We have certainly struck for the people in this Qur'an from every kind of example﴾ [al-Rum: 58]. This refers to what Allah deposited in His clear Book of various parables and diverse admonitions, and what this surah carried of that. Glorified is He followed that with His true saying: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim﴾ ﴿These are the verses of the Wise Book﴾, that is, its proofs and demonstrations, for those who are granted success and for whom the best (al-husna) has preceded, and they are the muhsinun whom He mentions after this. The description of the Book as "Wise" bears witness to what we have laid down. Then glorified is He pointed to those who are deprived of its benefit and of taking heed through it, who exchanged guidance for error and turned away from the ways of the natural disposition (fitrah) of Allah upon which He created people, and so He said: ﴿And among the people is one who purchases idle talk﴾ [Luqman: 6], and the verses that follow. Then He followed that with what rebukes every obstinate person and silences every denier. He mentioned the creation of the heavens without visible pillars, observable and witnessed, about which no one can doubt. Then He mentioned the creation of the earth and what He deposited in it. Then glorified is He said: ﴿This is the creation of Allah, so show me what those other than Him have created﴾ [Luqman: 11]. Then He followed that by mentioning the one whom He guided to the path of the natural disposition, so that doubts did not divert him and he did not deviate from the right way, and so He said: ﴿And We had certainly given Luqman wisdom﴾ [Luqman: 12], and the verse that follows, to establish those who followed the natural disposition of Allah, which was mentioned earlier in Surah al-Rum. Then the speech became coherent and interwoven. End.

Since ihsan (excellence in worship) is what the surah of al-Rum called for, namely faith in meeting Allah, exalted above all imperfection, described with the attributes of perfection, worshipped by what He has legislated, in sincerity and submission to the proof wherever it turns and in turning with it wherever it goes, and since that is the very essence of wisdom (hikmah), Allah the Exalted says: ﴿A guidance﴾, that is, while it is (or while it is the case that it is) a clear and firm exposition, ﴿and a mercy﴾, that is, bearing one to carry out everything it calls to. The construction according to the reading of Hamzah with the nominative is: "it is" or "it is" (p-144) "He is". [And] He says: ﴿for the good-doers﴾, indicating that among its wisdom is that it is specific to those who attain this perfection, placing the thing in its proper place by this category. They are those who held fast to taqwa (God-consciousness), which led them to ihsan, and ihsan is worshipping Allah as though seeing Him through unveiling (al-mukashafah) and watchfulness (al-muraqabah). So it is for Him, or He is its last (end), as one.

Then He described them, within the context of mercy, wisdom and clear explanation through justice, as a clarification for them of what Surat al-Rum called for regarding perfect excellence (ihsan) in dealing with the Truth and with creation, in belief and in action. So He said: ﴿Those who establish the prayer﴾, meaning they make it as though it were established by its performance, by means of perfecting all that was afterward commanded within it and recommended to it, and upon which it depends in some respect, in a renewed manner at its appropriate times and with continuity. The expression is not given in the form of the active participle such as "al-Muqimin" (the establishers), because there is no call for that, in order to indicate firmness (rusukh), since the one who performs excellence is the one firmly rooted in the religion, a firmness that makes him as though he sees the One worshipped. Included within it is the Hajj, for one who magnifies the House five times every day is none other than one who magnifies it through the Hajj, either in deed or in capacity. ﴿And who give the zakat﴾, meaning all of it, so fasting entered within it, for one does not pay the zakat of breaking the fast (zakat al-fitr) except one who has fasted, either in capacity or in deed.

Since faith is the foundation of these pillars, and since faith in the Resurrection encompasses all its kinds and drives all aspects of excellence, and since the Surah of the Romans had concluded with turning away at its root from one who does not have the capacity for certainty, He said: ﴿And they﴾, meaning specifically, ﴿in the Hereafter﴾ (al-akhirah), owing to their perfection in what they have entered into of these meanings, ﴿[and] of it﴾ — the Hereafter about which the criminals were previously said to be heedless — ﴿they are certain﴾, meaning they believe in it with the faith of one who is certain. So they do not perform any deed without faith in it, and they do not neglect it for the blink of an eye. Thus he is at the pinnacle of that, for he worships Allah as though he sees Him. So the verse of al-Baqarah is a beginning, and this is an end.

Since these qualities are the mothers of the actions that necessitate perfection, and since they are in some respect equivalent to the verse of al-Baqarah, he concluded it with its seal, after having reined it in with its bridle, saying: ﴿Those﴾, i.e., those of exalted rank who have attained the stations of nearness, are greater in rank, ﴿upon guidance﴾, i.e., a great guidance, they are firmly established in it with the firmness of one who is elevated above a thing, and He said: ﴿from their Lord﴾, as a reminder to them that, had it not been for His beneficence, they would not have reached anything, so that they would cling to rubbing their foreheads upon the thresholds, out of fear of self-admiration. ﴿And those﴾, i.e., exclusively, ﴿they are the successful﴾, i.e., those who attain every desired goal.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 31, verse 6:

When the weaning of the soul from desires becomes the greatest guidance leading to the attainment of what is sought, and following them is the greatest cutter-off from perfections, and it is in the conclusion of Surat al-Rum that whoever stands with imaginings instead of seeking known truths, "is sealed upon his heart," and what the Book calls to is wisdom (ḥikmah), whose fruit is success, while what idle play calls to is folly (safah), which is the opposite of wisdom, by placing things in other than their proper places, and which yields ruin; God, Exalted is He, said, marvelling at those who abandon seriousness for idle play and turn away from the essence of knowledge to true heedlessness, linking it to what is implied in the sense: "Among people is one who adorns himself with this state and so rises to the arena of the people of perfection": ﴿And among people﴾. It is possible that this is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) of the subject of the demonstrative: I point to the verses of the Wise Book, being a guidance for those who remember, while among ﴿people﴾, those who are at the lowest rank of perception, have not reached the rank of the people of faith, let alone the station of the people of excellence.

Since the implied meaning is: whoever travels other than this journey, cutting his soul off from every good, He expressed this with His saying: ﴿whoever buys﴾ [i.e.] not guided by the Book nor shown mercy by it, ﴿idle talk﴾, i.e. what diverts among new and renewed things that one enjoys, by which one passes the time: singing, jokes, and everything without benefit, so that the soul, carried by the pleasure it has been led to, reaches the mere bestial nature, and then calls it to frivolous play, such as dancing and the like, striving in that, exerting horses in obtaining it by purchasing its cause, turning away from hunting sciences and refining the soul through them from worries and sorrows, so that it descends to the lowest of the low, just as the one before it ascended by wisdom to the highest of the high. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: it was revealed concerning a man who bought a slave-girl who sang to him night and day. Mujahid said: concerning the purchase of singing-girls, singers (male and female). Ibn Mas'ud said: idle play is singing, and so said Ibn 'Abbas and others.

Since it is known that the end of these diversions is misguidance, through the soul's absorption in them, because of its natural inclination toward mere idleness, how much more so with what stirs this and calls to it of pleasure, so that it becomes a captive of heedlessness from remembrance and a tribe turning away from reflection. The one addressed by this Book were a people who claimed superior intellects and pure, clear minds. God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿that he may mislead﴾, from misguidance and causing to go astray according to the two readings, the opposite of what the good-doers were upon of guidance ﴿from the way of God﴾, i.e. the clear, broad path that leads to the pleasure of the Supreme King, who combines [the attributes of] perfection, majesty and beauty, many of which they acknowledge, alerting them that this is certainly misleading from the way, and that this is such that it is not hidden from them; so if it is their intended aim, it is what no one counted among mankind would intend, and otherwise they are in a state of heedlessness, bad reasoning and blindness of insight, at a level far below that by many stages.

Since the purpose of intending to go astray from something is leaving that thing, and the intelligent person does not proceed to abandon something unless he knows that there is no good in it, He said: ﴿without knowledge﴾, indefinite to convey the general negation of every kind of knowledge, i.e. because they have no knowledge of anything of the state of the way nor the state of anything else, knowledge deserving the name of knowledge by being something that yields profit or preserves the capital of religion or worldly life; for this is the state of one who has exchanged falsehood for truth and misguidance for guidance.

Since the one who mocks a thing he despises cannot do so except after complete experience of that thing's condition, and that it is not fit for its proper use nor brings value to its owner, state after state, He said, marvelling at it with a second, greater marvelling than the first, in the accusative as a coordination with "yaḍill" in the reading of Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs from 'Asim, and in the nominative for the rest, coordinating with ﴿yashtari﴾: ﴿and take it﴾, i.e. he burdens himself against what his [original] nature calls him to, that he take the path than which none is nobler, together with the absolute ignorance established for him: ﴿as a mockery﴾.

Since this act produced for him perpetual wretchedness, He explained it by His saying, collectively, in accordance with the meaning of "man" after having used the singular in accordance with its wording, because the plural in the context of recompense is more terrible, and marvelling at the singular is more eloquent: ﴿Those﴾, i.e. the dullards far removed from the rank of humanity, and the phrasing with the preposition "lām", which is used for what is fitting, mocks them, so He said: ﴿for them is a humiliating punishment﴾, i.e. lasting disgrace is established for them, the opposite of the mercy that was for the good-doers.

Since man may be heedless, and when he is reminded he becomes attentive, God, glorified is He, indicated that this man, who is immersed in the causes of loss, does not increase over the passage of time except in defiance of every proof that reaches him, through rebellion and transgression. So He said, using the singular for the pronoun, following the wording (also) lest someone make a far-fetched claim that what is blameworthy is only the plural, and turning the speech toward the manifestation of majesty, as the situation required of intimidation (al-tarhib, frightening warning):

(p-150) ﴿And when Our verses are recited to him﴾, meaning: the recitation of them continually reaches him, together with their majesty, by whatever reciter it is, however great he may be. ﴿He turns away﴾, meaning: after hearing, he turns away in every sense, whether in a state of avoidance or [turning his back]. ﴿Arrogantly﴾, meaning: while he is seeking to make it exist by turning away from obedience, confirming Our saying at the end of that (verse): ﴿And if you brought them a sign, those who disbelieved would surely say, "You are only practitioners of falsehood."﴾ [al-Rum: 58]

Since the one who hears His verses, glorified is He, is worthy of being made tender and humble, He said, the Exalted, indicating that this wretched one's state, when he hears and when he is far away, was the same as it had been before: ﴿As if﴾, meaning: as if he were, that is, his state after hearing is made similar to his state when ﴿he did not hear it﴾. This shows that he never ceased to be in a state of arrogance, because He likened his state with hearing to his state without hearing, and He had made clear that his state with hearing is arrogance, so his state before hearing was likewise.

Since one who has not heard a thing may be receptive to hearing, so that when someone from whom hearing is customarily expected speaks to him, he hears, He made clear that the state of this person, just as it was equal to what was before the recitation, is equal to what is after it, because his hearing resembles that of one who has deafness. Thus the present tense in "is recited" conveys that the state in the future is like the state in the present. So He, the Exalted, said: ﴿As if there were deafness in his ears﴾, meaning: a deafness in which his being addressed by others and his silence are equal.

(p-151) Since this led to his deserving what would remove his haughtiness, pride and greatness, and since the persistence of pain is the greatest breaker of the proud, and since it is in human nature to be stirred by the promise of kindness, whoever he may be, He said: ﴿So give him good tidings﴾. Since he was worthy of turning toward it (the good news), not turning away due to his human assumption, toward its reality, because one who knows that he deserves punishment for his grievous deeds keeps having favors follow him again and again, until he assumes, or almost decides, that sins are the cause of this, and that he, because of his great rank with God, has no deed of his that is disliked. He rebuked him with His saying: ﴿with a painful punishment﴾, meaning: a continuous retribution.

When the knowledge of what belongs to one of the two groups prompts questioning about what belongs to the other group, and answering that question is among the most complete wisdom, the Exalted continued His speech, emphasizing it to counter the disbelievers' denial: ﴿Indeed, those who believe﴾ — they brought faith into existence — ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ — that is, as confirmation of it (al-taṣdīq lahu) — ﴿righteous deeds﴾ — placing a thing in its proper place, acting in accordance with wisdom (al-ḥikmah) — ﴿for them are gardens﴾ — that is, orchards — ﴿of bliss﴾. By attributing them to Himself, He, glorified is He, conveyed that there is no turbidity (kadar) in them whatsoever, and nothing other than bliss.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 31, verse 9:

When that may not be perpetual, and there is no joy in something that is cut off, he said: ﴿Abiding therein forever﴾, meaning, perpetually.

Since confidence in a promise is in proportion to confidence in the one who promises, and fulfilling a promise is part of wisdom, he said, emphasizing the content of the promise of the gardens: ﴿The promise of Allah﴾, which is such that nothing is more majestic than Him; so there is no promise more truthful than His promise. Then he reinforced it with his saying: ﴿in truth﴾, meaning, firmly established with a firmness for which there is nothing like it, because it is the promise of One to whom nothing is like and who has no equal.

Since the strange soul is worthy of emphasis, he brought two attributes, from what the mention of the Divine Name (al-Jalalah) conveys, stating them explicitly as emphasis, because this is indispensable. So he said: ﴿And He is﴾, meaning, He promised this while being ﴿the Almighty (al-'Aziz)﴾, so nothing overcomes Him, ﴿the All-Wise (al-Hakim)﴾, meaning, the One who perfects what He says and does, so that it cannot be annulled or diminished.

When He concluded with the two attributes of might, which is the furthest reach of power, and wisdom, which is the fruit of knowledge, He pointed to them through the perfection and firm construction of His acts, saying: ﴿He created the heavens﴾, i.e., upon their height, their greatness and their vastness, ﴿without pillars﴾. His saying ﴿that you see﴾ indicates wisdom, whether we say it is an attribute of "pillars" or a resumptive clause (*istinaf*, a new sentence that does not grammatically depend on what precedes it). If we take the second, then it is because such a great, vast creation bears itself by sheer power. If we take the first, then the erection of such a thing upon pillars, which customarily would bear it, yet which are such that they are not seen, is more deeply within wisdom and more subtle in refinement and greatness, because it requires two works: lightening the dense and strengthening the subtle. (p-153)

When He mentioned the pillars, which are few, He followed them with the stabilizing pegs, saying: ﴿And He cast on the earth﴾, i.e., the earth on which you are, ﴿firm mountains﴾. The wonder is from above them; all the firm mountains you know are from beneath, holding them ﴿lest it shake﴾, i.e., lest it sway and tremble ﴿with you﴾, as is the case with what is on the surface of water.

When He mentioned their creation and their arrangement for stability, He mentioned what they were created for from among the animals, saying: ﴿And He dispersed in it﴾, i.e., scattered, ﴿every kind of creature﴾. When He mentioned that, He mentioned what they live by, alerting, by way of the manifestation of greatness, to the fact that although they have some causative part in it, none can do it but He, glory be to Him. Saying: ﴿And We sent down﴾, i.e., by what We have of might, which necessarily accompanies power, and He put first what no creature has power over in any respect, saying: ﴿from the sky, water﴾. Since the arrangement of sustenance follows from that, and it is among the effects of wisdom that follows the work, He indicated it by His saying: ﴿then We caused to grow﴾, i.e., by what We have of exaltedness in wisdom, ﴿in it﴾, i.e., in the earth, by mixing the water with its soil, ﴿every kind of pair﴾, i.e., a type of plant similar to the others, ﴿noble﴾, by what it has of beauty and freshness, which bring joy and benefit, and of abundance which preserves those creatures.

When the Creation's greatness in this firmly established form proved His might and wisdom, His divinity was also established. So He obligated them to affirm His oneness in worship just as He is singular in creation, because that is the very essence of wisdom, just as His creating this creation in this order was so that the secret of wisdom would point to Him, glory be to Him. So He said, instructing the righteous of His party what they may use to admonish the opponents, rebuking them and condemning their state in turning away from Him despite their knowledge of His singularity in these works: ﴿This﴾ [i.e., all of what you witness] ﴿is the creation of Allah﴾, i.e., the One to whom belongs all greatness, so there is no equal to Him.

Since a rational being, and indeed any other being, does not submit to anything unless it sees in it an act that necessitates submission to it, He drew attention to this by saying, as a reply to what is implied, namely: If you claim for what is other than Him, which you have worshipped besides Him, a creation for which you worship it: ﴿Then show me what those beside Him have created﴾. He added the demonstrative as an increase in rebuke, to emphasize the negation intended by the speech, and He drew attention to the lowliness of their rank by saying, using the pronoun because there is no attribute ascribed to the Greatest Name in which a qualification feared to be deficient could arise: ﴿beside Him﴾. So He asked them to see what they created, and no one would be deceived at all, by submitting to what cannot be submitted to by any animal, let alone a human, since it has no act whatsoever. Therefore it was incumbent upon you, if you have intellects, to investigate first whether they have acts or not; then, once established, whether those acts are firm or not; then, once established, whether others shared with them or not; and, if it is established that others shared with them, which of them is more firm. As for your submitting to them while they have no act at all, and then supposing that they have acts by which you hope for them and fear them, this is something no animal could conceive at all. Therefore Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Rather﴾, drawing attention to the fact that the answer is: they have no creation. Rather, their worshippers, or you, in making them partners [are the ones who err]. This was the original form, but He said: ﴿the wrongdoers﴾, i.e., those who are extreme in wrongdoing, as a generalization and an alert to the attribute that made it necessary for them to be ﴿in error﴾, very great and encompassing them, ﴿clear﴾, i.e., in the utmost clarity, which is that they place things out of their place through mountains of desire, so there is no wisdom in them.

ولَمّا ثَبَتَتْ حِكْمَتُهُ سُبْحانَهُ وأنَّهُ أبْعَدَهم عَنْها بِما قَضى عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ الجَهْلِ وغَباوَةِ العَقْلِ وآتاها مَن تابَ، واعْتَصَمَ بِآياتِ الكِتابِ، تَوَقَّعَ السّامِعُ الإخْبارَ عَنْ بَعْضِ مَن آتاهُ الحِكْمَةَ مِنَ المُتَقَدِّمِينَ الَّذِينَ كانُوا مِنَ المُحْسِنِينَ، فَوَضَعُوا الأشْياءَ في مَواضِعِها بِأنْ آمَنُوا عَلى قَوْلِهِ: "وهُوَ العَزِيزُ الحَكِيمُ" أوْ عَلى مُقَدَّرٍ تَقْدِيرُهُ: لِأنّا أضْلَلْناهم بِحِكْمَتِنا وآتَيْنا الحِكْمَةَ الَّذِينَ قَبِلُوا آياتِنا وأحْسَنُوا التَّعَبُّدَ لَنا فَما عَبَدُوا صَنَمًا ولا مالُوا إلى لَهْوٍ، لِأنَّ ذَلِكَ عَيْنُ الحِكْمَةِ لِكَوْنِهِ [وضْعًا] لِلشَّيْءِ في مَحَلِّهِ، فَهو (p-١٥٦) تَقْدِيرٌ لِتَخْصِيصِ النَّبِيِّ (ﷺ) بِالرِّسالَةِ: ﴿ولَقَدْ آتَيْنا﴾ أي: ولقد أعطينا، بِما لَنا مِنَ العَظْمَةِ والحِكْمَةِ ﴿لُقْمانَ﴾ وهو عَبْدٌ مِن عَبِيدِنا ﴿الحِكْمَةَ﴾ وهو العِلْمُ المُؤَيَّدُ بِالعَمَلِ، والعَمَلُ المُحْكَمُ بِالعِلْمِ، وقالَ الحَرالِيُّ: هي العِلْمُ بِالأمْرِ الَّذِي لِأجْلِهِ وجَبَ الحُكْمُ، والحُكْمُ الحَمْلُ عَلى جَمِيعِ أنْواعِ الصَّبْرِ والمُصابَرَةِ ظاهِرًا بِالإيالَةِ العالِيَةِ، ولا يَتِمُّ الحُكْمُ وتَسْتَوِي الحِكْمَةُ إلّا بِحَسَبِ سَعَةِ العِلْمِ، وقالَ ابْنُ مَيْلَقٍ: إنَّ مَدارَها عَلى إصابَةِ الحَقِّ والصَّوابِ في القَوْلِ [والعَمَلِ]، ولِهَذا قالَ ابْنُ قُتَيْبَةَ: لا يُقالُ لِشَخْصٍ حَكِيمًا حَتّى تَجْتَمِعَ لَهُ الحِكْمَةُ في القَوْلِ والفِعْلِ، قالَ: ولا يُسَمّى المُتَكَلِّمُ بِالحِكْمَةِ حَكِيمًا حَتّى يَكُونَ عامِلًا بِها. انْتَهى.

ومِن بَلِيغِ حِكْمَتِهِ ما أسْنَدَهُ صاحِبُ الفِرْدَوْسِ عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُما أنَّ النَّبِيَّ (ﷺ) قالَ: «حَقًّا أقُولُ! لَمْ يَكُنْ لُقْمانُ نَبِيًّا، ولَكِنْ كانَ عَبْدًا ضَمْضامَةً كَثِيرَ التَّفَكُّرِ حَسَنَ اليَقِينِ، أحَبَّ اللَّهَ فَأحَبَّهُ، فَمَنَّ عَلَيْهِ بِالحِكْمَةِ، كانَ نائِمًا نِصْفَ النَّهارِ إذْ جاءَهُ نِداءٌ، قِيلَ: يا لُقْمانُ، هَلْ لَكَ أنْ يَجْعَلَكَ اللَّهُ خَلِيفَةً في الأرْضِ تَحْكُمُ بَيْنَ النّاسِ بِالحَقِّ، فَأجابَ: إنْ خَيَّرَنِي رَبِّي قَبِلْتُ العافِيَةَ ولَمْ أقْبَلِ البَلاءَ، وإنْ عَزَمَ عَلَيَّ فَسَمْعًا وطاعَةً، فَإنِّي أعْلَمُ أنَّهُ إنْ فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ رَبِّي عَصَمَنِي وأعانَنِي، فَقالَتِ المَلائِكَةُ بِصَوْتٍ لا يَراهُمْ: (p-١٥٧) لِمَ يا لُقْمانُ؟ قالَ: لِأنَّ الحاكِمَ بِأشَدِّ المَنازِلِ وأكْدَرِها، يَغْشاهُ الظُّلْمُ مِن كُلِّ مَكانٍ، إذْ يَعْدِلُ فَبِالحَرِيِّ أنْ يَنْجُوَ، وإنْ أخْطَأ أخْطَأ طَرِيقَ الجَنَّةِ، ومَن يَكُنْ في الدُّنْيا ذَلِيلًا خَيْرٌ مِن أنْ يَكُونَ شَرِيفًا، ومَن تَخَيَّرَ الدُّنْيا عَلى الآخِرَةِ تَفْتِنْهُ الدُّنْيا ولا يُصِيبُ الآخِرَةَ، فَعَجِبَتِ المَلائِكَةُ مِن حُسْنِ مَنطِقِهِ، فَنامَ نَوْمَةً فَأُعْطِيَ الحِكْمَةَ فانْتَبَهَ يَتَكَلَّمُ بِها». وفي الفِرْدَوْسِ عَنْ مَكارِمِ الأخْلاقِ لِأبِي بَكْرِ بْنِ هِلالٍ عَنْ أبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ أنَّ النَّبِيَّ (ﷺ) [قالَ]: «الحِكْمَةُ عَشَرَةُ أجْزاءٍ تِسْعَةٌ مِنها في العُزْلَةِ وواحِدٌ في الصَّمْتِ»، [وقالَ لُقْمانُ]: لا مالَ كَصِحَّةٍ ولا نَعِيمَ كَطِيبِ نَفْسٍ، وقالَ: ضَرْبُ الوالِدِ لِوَلَدِهِ كالسَّماءِ لِلزَّرْعِ، وقِيلَ لَهُ: أيُّ النّاسِ شَرٌّ؟ قالَ: الَّذِي لا يُبالِي أنْ يَراهُ النّاسُ مُسِيئًا، وقِيلَ لَهُ: ما أقْبَحَ وجْهَكَ! فَقالَ: تَعِيبُ النَّقْشَ أوِ النَّقّاشَ، وقالَ البَغَوِيُّ: إنَّهُ قِيلَ لَهُ: لِمَ بَلَغْتَ ما بَلَغْتَ؟ قالَ: بِصِدْقِ الحَدِيثِ وأداءِ الأمانَةِ وتَرْكِ ما لا يَعْنِينِي. انْتَهى. فَهو سُبْحانَهُ مِن حِكْمَتِهِ وحِكَمِهِ أنْ يَرْفَعَ ما يَشاءُ بِما يَعْلَمُهُ مِنهُ مِن سَلامَةِ الطَّبْعِ، وإنْ كانَ عَبْدًا فَلا بِدْعَ أنْ يَخْتَصَّ (p-١٥٨) مُحَمَّدًا (ﷺ) ذا النَّسَبِ العالِي والمَنصِبِ المُنِيفِ في كُلِّ خَلْقٍ شَرِيفٍ بِالرِّسالَةِ مِن بَيْنِ قُرَيْشٍ، وإنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ مِن أهْلِ الدُّنْيا المُتَعَظِّمِينَ بِها، قالَ ابْنُ مَيْلَقٍ: مِن حِكْمَتِهِ سُبْحانَهُ أنْ يَجْمَعَ بَيْنَ أثَرَيْ عَدْلِهِ وفَضْلِهِ، وأنْ يُعاقِبَ بَيْنَهُما في الظُّهُورِ فَيُذِلَّ ويُعِزَّ ويُفْقِرَ ويُغْنِيَ ويُسْقِمَ ويَشْفِيَ ويُفْنِيَ ويُبْقِيَ إلى غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ، فَما مِن سابِقِ عَدْلٍ إلّا لَهُ لاحِقُ فَضْلٍ، ولا سابِقِ فَضْلٍ إلّا لَهُ لاحِقُ عَدْلٍ، غَيْرَ أنَّ أثَرَ العَدْلِ والفَضْلِ قَدْ يَتَعَلَّقُ بِالبَواطِنِ خاصَّةً، وقَدْ يَتَعَلَّقُ أحَدُهُما بِالظّاهِرِ والآخِرُ بِالباطِنِ، وقَدْ يَكُونُ اخْتِلافُ تَعَلُّقِهِما في حالَةٍ واحِدَةٍ، وقَدْ يَكُونُ عَلى البَدَلِ، وعَلى قَدْرِ تَعَلُّقِ الأثَرِ [السّابِقِ يَكُونُ تَعَلُّقُ الأثَرِ] اللّاحِقِ.

ولَمّا كانَتِ الحِكْمَةُ قاضِيَةً بِذَلِكَ، أجْرى اللَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ آثارَ عَدْلِهِ عَلى ظَواهِرِ أصْفِيائِهِ دُونَ بَواطِنِهِمْ، ثُمَّ عَقَّبَتْ ذَلِكَ بِإيرادِ آثارِ فَضْلِهِ عَلى بَواطِنِهِمْ وظَواهِرِهِمْ حَتّى صارَ مِن قاعِدَةِ الحِكْمَةِ الإلَهِيَّةِ تَفْوِيضُ مَمالِكِ الأرْضِ لِلْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ فِيها كالنَّجاشِيِّ حَيْثُ بِيعَ في صِغَرِهِ، وذَلِكَ كَثِيرٌ مَوْجُودٌ بِالِاسْتِقْراءِ، فَمِن كَمالِ تَرْبِيَةِ الحَكِيمِ لِمَن يُرِيدُ إعْلاءَ شَأْنِهِ أنْ يَجْرِيَ عَلى ظاهِرِهِ مِن أثَرِ العَدْلِ ما فِيهِ تَكْمِيلٌ لَهم وتَنْوِيرٌ لِمَدارِكِهِمْ وتَطْهِيرٌ لِوُجُودِهِمْ وتَهْذِيبٌ وتَأْدِيبٌ، إلى غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ مِن فَوائِدِ التَّرْبِيَةِ، ومَن تَتَبُّعِ أحْوالِ الأكابِرِ مِن آدَمَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ وهَلُمَّ جَرًّا رَأى مِن حُسْنِ (p-١٥٩) بَلاءِ اللَّهِ سُبْحانَهُ وتَعالى لَهم ما يَشْهَدُ لِما قَرَّرَتْهُ بِالصِّحَّةِ إنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ تَعالى. انْتَهى.

ولَمّا كانَتِ الحِكْمَةُ هي الإقْبالُ عَلى اللَّهِ قالَ: ﴿أنِ اشْكُرْ﴾ وهو وإنْ كانَ تَقْدِيرُهُ: قُلْنا لَهُ كَذا، يُؤَوَّلُ إلى "آتَيْناهُ الشُّكْرَ"، وصُرِفَ الكَلامُ إلى الِاسْمِ الأعْظَمِ (al-ism al-a'zam: the greatest name of God) الَّذِي لَمْ يَتَسَمَّ بِهِ غَيْرُهُ سُبْحانَهُ دَفْعًا لِلتَّعَنُّتِ، ونَقْلًا عَنْ مَظْهَرِ العَظَمَةِ [إلى] أعْظَمَ مِنها فَقالَ: ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ بِأنْ وفَّقْناهُ لَهُ بِما سَبَّبْناهُ لَهُ مِنَ الأمْرِ بِهِ، لِأنَّ الحِكْمَةَ في الحَقِيقَةِ هي القِيامُ بِالشُّكْرِ لا الإيصاءُ بِهِ، ويُمْكِنُ أنْ تَكُونَ "أنْ" مَصْدَرِيَّةً، ويَكُونُ التَّقْدِيرُ: آتَيْناهُ إيّاها بِسَبَبِ الشُّكْرِ، وعَبَّرَ بِفِعْلِ الأمْرِ إعْلامًا بِأنَّ شُكْرَهُ كانَ لِامْتِثالِ الأمْرِ لِيَكُونَ أعْلى.

ولَمّا كانَ التَّقْدِيرُ: فَبادَرَ وشَكَرَ، فَما نَفَعَ إلّا نَفْسَهُ، كَما أنَّهُ لَوْ كَفَرَ ما ضَرَّ إلّا نَفْسَهُ، عَطَفَ عَلَيْهِ [مُعَرِّفًا] أنَّهُ غَنِيٌّ عَنْ شُكْرِ الشّاكِرِينَ قَوْلَهُ مُعَبِّرًا بِالمُضارِعِ الدّالِّ عَلى أنَّ مَن أقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِ، في أيِّ زَمانٍ كانَ، يَلْقاهُ ويَكُونُ مَعْرُوفُهُ لَهُ دائِمًا بِدَوامِ العَمَلِ: ﴿ومَن يَشْكُرْ﴾ أيْ يُجَدِّدِ الشُّكْرَ ويَتَعاهَدْ بِهِ نَفْسَهُ كائِنًا مَن كانَ ﴿فَإنَّما يَشْكُرُ﴾ أيْ يَفْعَلُ ذَلِكَ ﴿لِنَفْسِهِ﴾ أيْ فَإنَّما يَنْفَعُ نَفْسَهُ، فَإنَّ اللَّهَ يَزِيدُهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ فَإنَّ اللَّهَ (p-١٦٠) شَكُورٌ مَجِيدٌ ﴿ومَن كَفَرَ﴾ فَإنَّما يَضُرُّ نَفْسَهُ، وعَبَّرَ بِالماضِي إشارَةً إلى أنَّ مَن وقَعَ مِنهُ كُفْرٌ ولَوْ مَرَّةً جُوزِيَ بِالإعْراضِ عَنْهُ ﴿فَإنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ عَبَّرَ بِالِاسْمِ الأعْظَمِ لِأنَّهُ في سِياقِ الحِكْمَةِ، والحَكِيمُ مَن أدامَ اسْتِحْضارَ صِفاتِ الجَلالِ والجَمالِ فَغَلَبَ خَوْفُهُ رَجاءَهُ ما دامَ في دارِ الأكْدارِ ﴿غَنِيٌّ﴾ عَنِ الشُّكْرِ وغَيْرِهِ ﴿حَمِيدٌ﴾ أيْ لَهُ جَمِيعُ المَحامِدِ وإنْ كَفَرَهُ جَمِيعُ الخَلائِقِ، فَإنَّ تَقْدِيرَ الكُفْرِ عَلَيْهِمْ بِحَيْثُ لا يَقْدِرُونَ عَلى الِانْفِكاكِ عَنْهُ مِن جُمْلَةِ مَحامِدِهِ بِالقُدْرَةِ والعِزَّةِ والفَهْمِ والعَظَمَةِ. ويَجُوزُ، وهو أقْرَبُ، أنْ يَعُودَ "غَنِيٌّ" إلى الكافِرِ و"حَمِيدٌ" إلى الشّاكِرِ، فَيَكُونُ اسْمَ فاعِلٍ، فَيَكُونُ التَّقْدِيرُ: ومَن كَفَرَ فَإنَّما يَكْفُرُ عَلى نَفْسِهِ، ثُمَّ سَبَّبَ عَنِ الجُمْلَتَيْنِ و[هُما] كَوْنُ عَمَلِ كُلٍّ مِنَ الشّاكِرِ والكافِرِ لا يَتَعَدّاهُ قَوْلُهُ "فَإنَّ اللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ" [أيْ] عَنْ شُكْرِ الكافِرِ "حَمِيدٌ" لِلشّاكِرِ، والآيَةُ عَلى الأوَّلِ مِنَ الِاحْتِباكِ: تَخْصِيصُ الشُّكْرِ بِالنَّفْسِ أوَّلًا يَدُلُّ عَلى حَذْفِ مِثْلِهِ مِنَ الكُفْرِ ثانِيًا، وإثْباتِ الصِّفَتَيْنِ يَدُلُّ عَلى حَذْفِ مِثْلِهِما أوَّلًا.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 31, verse 13:

Since a person cannot know the wisdom of the wise except through his sayings and actions, and cannot know the truthfulness and wisdom [of speech] except through its conformity to reality, the sense is: Mention what We have described Luqman with, so that what you hear of his conditions and actions may apply to you, in fulfilling the right of God and the right of the creatures, which is the axis of wisdom. Then He joined to it His words: ﴿And when﴾, meaning: And mention with your heart, so that you may take admonition, and with your tongue, so that you may admonish others, insofar as you are a Messenger, what occurred when ﴿Luqman said to his son﴾, which indicates his thankfulness in himself and his command to others to be thankful. For there is no thankfulness equal to disavowing association (shirk). In it is also an exhortation to adopt the qualities for which Luqman was praised, which lead to patience, thankfulness, and persistence in every good, and to the disciplining of a child by framing speech in a way that indicates the repetition of his admonition. So He said: ﴿while he was admonishing him﴾, meaning: advising him with what benefits him, softens his heart, refines his soul, and instills in him fear (of God) and justice.

Since the foundation of fulfilling the right of the Truth is correcting belief (i'tiqad) and reforming action, and the first is more important, he placed it first, saying: ﴿O my son﴾. He addressed him with the most beloved address, together with showing mercy, tenderness, and compassion, so that this would be more conducive to the acceptance of counsel. ﴿Do not associate﴾, meaning: do not commit association (shirk), neither openly nor secretly. Since diminutive address (al-tasghir) implies compassion for him, this was increased by mentioning the Greatest Name, which necessitates the summoning of all majesty, to confirm greater compassion. So he said: ﴿with God﴾, meaning: the Greatest King, who has no equal. Then he gave the reason for this prohibition in His words: ﴿Indeed, association﴾, meaning in both its kinds, ﴿is a great injustice﴾, meaning: it is the opposite of wisdom, because it is placing a thing in other than its proper place. Its injustice is evident from very many aspects, the most evident of which is that it equates the created being, who has in himself nothing but non-existence, with the Originator of blessing, the Owner who possesses necessary existence (wujub al-wujud). There is no good and no blessing except from Him. In this there is an alert to the Quraysh and to every listener that this is an injunction not to be turned away from, because it comes from a wise father to a beloved son whom he cherishes, and that their forefathers, had they been wise, would have done nothing but this. For upon it depends what the blessings, both apparent and hidden, religious and worldly, immediate and deferred, rest on, namely security and guidance: ﴿Those who believe and do not mix their belief with injustice—for them is security, and they are rightly guided﴾ [al-An'am: 82]. For when that verse was revealed, as is in Sahih al-Bukhari in more than one place, on the authority of ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud (may Allah be pleased with him), it weighed heavily upon the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them), and they said: "Which of us has not mixed his belief with injustice?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is not that. Have you not heard the words of Luqman: ﴿Indeed, association is a great injustice﴾?"

When He, glory be to Him, mentioned what Luqman had enjoined on his son, namely thanks to the First Benefactor, to whom no one shares in bringing things into existence, and mentioned how grave, monstrous and abhorrent associating partners with Him is, He, glory be to Him, followed that with His charge to the child concerning the parent. This is because the parent is the second benefactor, and God alone, glory be to Him, is the one who made the parent the cause of the child's existence. This acknowledges the truth, even if the child is still young in the eyes of his family. It also serves as a notice that whoever does not thank people does not thank God. It magnifies the right of the two parents, since He joined disobedience to them with associating partners with Him. And it informs us that fidelity is one thing: when any part of it is lacking, the rest of it collapses. This is as in the Firdaws (a hadith collection) on the authority of Abu al-Darda, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If a servant meets God with the full completion of what He made obligatory upon him, but without dutifulness to his parents, he will not enter Paradise. Indeed, dutifulness to parents is the foundation of monotheism, prayer and remembrance." For this reason the speech turned to the manifestation of greatness (ʿaẓamah), as a warning against disobedience to parents and as a removal of what might be imagined, namely that separating oneself from associating partners can only be achieved by turning away from all creation.

And because Satan may suggest that being bound to obey a parent is associating partners with God, that charge included Luqman's excellence (peace be upon him) in making thanks beautiful and associating partners ugly, in agreement with the command of the Lord of the Worlds, and in making it obligatory for his son to comply with his command. So He said, explaining the parent's right and the right of every other parent, and making known the ugliness of whoever commands his son to associate partners with God, because that contradicts the wisdom which Luqman (peace be upon him) expounded. It also prohibits the son from complying with that, and makes it obligatory for him to oppose his father in that matter, giving priority to the greater of two rights and committing the lesser of two harms: ﴿And We enjoined﴾, that is, Luqman said that to his son, advising him, while the state of affairs was that (We, in Our greatness, enjoined his son about it in a manner similar to what he had enjoined him concerning Our right. This is how the original would have been, but) He expressed it in a way that includes others, so He said: ﴿man﴾, that is, this species, through the tongue of the first prophet We sent, and so on, and by what We placed in every natural disposition (fitrah), namely that the reward of goodness is only goodness: ﴿to his parents﴾. It is as if He said: Luqman recognised Our blessing upon him and upon the sons of his kind, by Our enjoining upon their children (dutifulness) toward them. So he gave thanks, and on Our behalf he instructed them, through that, to forbid associating partners with God, because it is ingratitude for the blessing of the Benefactor. So he obeyed in himself and forbade his son, and thereby he was wise.

Since the mother is in a position of being belittled in comparison with the greatness of the father, in terms of strength, intellect, and the toil he undergoes for her and for their child, He highlighted her, and drew attention to what is specific to her among the causes of the child's existence and survival, beyond the father, from the hardship she endured because of him and from the upbringing that is due to her. So He said, giving a reason or beginning a new statement: ﴿His mother bore him in weakness﴾, that is, while she was in a state of weakness, carrying him in her womb. He exaggerated by making her very act the weakness itself, to show the intensity of that weakness, since it doubles each time she grows heavier. ﴿Upon weakness﴾, that is, it persists in her from the very creation and make-up of her body, to what increases her burden as the carrying continues. Then He pointed to the favour she bestowed upon him through compassion and good nurturing, while he himself owns nothing, by His saying: ﴿and his weaning﴾, that is, his being weaned from breastfeeding after his birth.

Since parents consider finding a child to be among the greatest causes of goodness and joy, He expressed the matter of weaning with the word *ʿām* (year), whose root revolves around abundance, in order to suit this, and as a consolation to them, being sustained by him and magnifying their right by using an expression that points to the difficulty they endured across an extended period. So He said: ﴿in two years﴾, during which she bears, in his sleeping and waking, what none knows its full extent except God, exalted is He. In the use of the word *ʿām* there is also an indication of the magnitude of its end-point, in that she counts the days of his suckling, even though they are the time when she is at her weakest in his upbringing, as days of abundance and joy. The use of *fī* (in) indicates that the two parents may wean him before the two years are complete, according to what his condition can bear and what the benefit of the matter calls for.

When He mentioned the charge and pointed to the principal causes of it, He mentioned the thing enjoined, and so He said, explaining ﴿We enjoined﴾: ﴿that give thanks﴾. Since gratitude is viewed in its most complete aspect, its verb is left without an object, that is: bring this reality into being and let it be among your concerns. Since it must have an object, it is as if He said: To whom? So He mentioned first what is the foundation of what is enjoined concerning the parents, so that it may be taken into account, and He directed the speech to the pronoun of the singular, without exalting it, in order to specify the intended meaning: ﴿to Me﴾, that is, because I am truly the Benefactor; ﴿and to your parents﴾, because I made them the cause of your existence and of the goodness of your upbringing. He mentioned the human being with this mention in the sura of Luqman (Wisdom), to indicate that he is the most perfect of created beings in wisdom. Al-Razi said at the end of the sura of al-Ahzab in his *Lawami*: All created beings are like a tree, and the human being is its fruit; they are like its husks, and the human being is its kernel; they are like its beginnings, and the human being is its perfection. How could the world possess what the human being possesses? Rather, the higher world is in him, while the higher world does not contain what is in him. He has combined the two worlds in his soul and body, gathered the two realms in his intellect and senses, and risen above both levels through the connection of the supreme command to him by revelation spoken, and he has submitted to the One to whom belong creation and command, in a voluntary, willing submission.

Then He gave the reason for the command to give thanks, warning, and said: ﴿To Me﴾, not to other than Me, ﴿is the final return﴾, that is: So I will question you about that, just as the beginning of creation was from them both, apparently, through the means I placed in them for that. So they will ask you about fulfilling their rights, and if you fell short in them, they will complain of you to the people and establish the proof against you and take their right from you.

[p-167] When Allah, glorified is He, mentioned His command concerning the two parents and affirmed their right, He followed it with the proof for what Luqman (peace be upon him) mentioned about the ugliness of shirk (associating partners with God). He said: ﴿But if they strive with you﴾, that is, to make you obey them in spite of what I have commanded you concerning obeying them. By the form of mufa'alah (the reciprocal form, "jahadaka"), He indicated their opposition, even if they exert great effort in pressing you to it, ﴿to make you associate with Me﴾. By the particle of elevation ("ʿalā"), He indicated that whoever obeys them in this has no hope, even if only verbally, of being counted among the good-doers, even if the two parents are at the utmost height of rank and have the most power over the means of temptation for him. This differs from Surat al-ʿAnkabut, where the particle is for temptation in general and not for the strength of the unbelievers. There He used the particle of cause (lam al-ʿilla), indicating striving in general, sincere whether strong or weak. So in both places there is a kind of symbolic hint that if one is weak before them, he obeys with his tongue, and that does not take him out of faith, just as it takes him out here from the description of ihsan (excellence). For this reason, in the verse after this one He warned against hypocrisy for the sake of temptation. Allah, glorified is He, referred to following the evidence, by the judgment of the reason He bestowed, with justice and fairness, and said: ﴿of which you have no knowledge﴾, indicating that no branch of knowledge can point to any shirk by any kind of indication. Rather, all the sciences point to the oneness (tawhid) in the manner on which the intellects agree and which the transmitted reports from the prophets and messengers have consistently affirmed. As for the form that the people of atheism, with the doctrine of ittihad (unification of existence), called tawhid, it is enough to show that it is not a matter of knowledge, since they agree that it lies outside the bounds of reason and contradicts everything transmitted from the prophets, even if they confuse people by claiming to follow some verses, as my book on al-Fāriḍ (Ibn al-Fāriḍ) makes clear. No one can adopt this doctrine except after stripping away reason and denying transmission. No one has announced against himself the nullity of what they proclaimed against themselves. But ﴿whom Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾.

When He had established this in this wonderful manner, He said, as a consequence of it: ﴿So do not obey them﴾, that is, in that, even if they unite to strive with you upon it. Rather, oppose them, and even if the matter leads to the sword, strive against them with it, because their command to that is contrary to wisdom, leading to pure injustice and folly. In this there is an admonition to the Quraysh regarding the sheer error of blindly following (taqlid) their forefathers in this.

Since this might suggest turning away from them entirely in every matter when they oppose them in religion, He indicated that this is not absolute, and said: ﴿and keep them company in this world﴾, that is, in their worldly affairs that do not relate to religion, as long as they are alive.

Since one built on deficiency is incapable of fulfilling all rights, He made it lighter for him by using the indefinite in His saying: ﴿kindly﴾, that is, by treating them well if they are upon a religion that they hold to, and by dealing with them with forbearance, tolerance, and what the noble character and high qualities require. Ibn Maylaq said: From this lamp there shines the glorification of the shaykhs who were customarily a means of bringing hearts into the circles of tawhid, both in knowledge and in practice. [p-169] That is: in presenting this command in this manner there is the greatest admonition that glorifying the intermediaries among creation is not a barrier to sincerity in tawhid. Ibn Maylaq said: From here the feet of peoples slipped who went to extremes in claiming tawhid, until they turned away from the side of intermediaries and fell into unbelief from the very place they thought was tawhid. Glorifying what is glorified in the Sharia is glorifying the sanctities of Allah and obeying the command of Allah. By my life, this slip is one over which the followers of Iblis stumble, since he refused to prostrate to other than Allah. Then he said something to the effect of: These are people who turned away from glorifying intermediaries, claiming zeal for the station of tawhid. Opposed to them are people who discarded intermediaries entirely and said: There is nothing in existence but Him. They are the people of absolute unity. All of them are upon error. The truth is moderation and justice in affirming the Creator and His oneness, and in glorifying those whom He commanded to be glorified among His servants.

Since this might lead to a kind of weakness in religion through some partiality, He negated that by His saying: ﴿And follow﴾, that is, strive hard to follow ﴿the way﴾, that is, the religion and path ﴿of one who turns back﴾, that is, who came submitting ﴿to Me﴾, not turning toward the worship of other than Me. They are the sincere ones among your two parents and others. For that does not take you out of their goodness, nor out of the tawhid of Allah and sincerity toward Him. In this there is an exhortation to recognize men by the truth, and a command to test the shaykhs and others by the touchstone of the Book and the Sunnah. Whoever's deed agrees with them is followed, and whoever's deed opposes them is avoided.

Since the implication is: indeed, the return of all your affairs in this world is to Me, He followed it with His saying: ﴿Then to Me﴾, that is, in the Hereafter, not to other than Me is your return. This was the original form, but He gathered it to express generality, and said, expressing it with the mimi verbal noun that denotes the event and its time and place: ﴿your return﴾, both physically and in meaning, so I will uncover the veil. ﴿And I will inform you﴾, that is, I will act as one who thoroughly investigates and informs, immediately after that and because of it, since that is the most fitting thing for wisdom, though every matter is followed by what befits it. ﴿Of what you used to do﴾, of what is for you like a natural disposition, ﴿you used to do﴾, that is, you renewed its doing from small and great, from grand and trivial, and what was in your natures and did not come out into the open. Then I will reward whom I will and forgive whom I will. So prepare its provision for it, and do not act like one who has no return in which he will be called to account and recompensed for the weight of an atom of his deeds. Perhaps He expressed reckoning as informing because knowledge of the deed is the cause of recompense for it, or because He gathered both kinds. The reckoning of the blessed one is merely the presentation, by implication (dalalat al-tadammun), while the reckoning of the wretched is by direct correspondence (al-mutabaqa).

(p-171) When Luqman, peace be upon him, had finished affirming what he had said about gratitude and shirk, and thus had known what wisdom he had been given, and he concluded it, after the counsel to obey one's parents, by mentioning fine and great deeds, and that they are equal in the knowledge of Allah, it was very fitting to return to the complete explanation of his wisdom. So he began with what is suitable to that, from the fine knowledge and its all-encompassing nature which completes the station of tawhid (divine oneness). He expressed it with "the weight of a mustard seed," because it is the least that generally comes to mind, and it is among the greatest incentives to tawhid whose foundation has already been laid: ﴿O my dear son﴾, showing affection and seeking to win him over, diminishing him in relation to bearing any part of the anger of Allah the Exalted, as one who is weak. ﴿Indeed, it﴾, that is, the deed, and it is feminine because it is in the position of diminishing and belittling, and the feminine is more appropriate for that, and because it is interpreted as obedience and disobedience, good deed and bad deed. ﴿If it be﴾, and he dropped the nun for the purpose of brevity in advising what brings success, and to indicate the least and smallest existence: ﴿the weight of﴾, that is, a weight. Then he belittled it by saying: ﴿a grain﴾, and he increased this by saying: ﴿of a mustard seed﴾. This is according to the reading of the majority with the accusative. The two Madinan readers read it in the nominative, in the sense that the matter and the great affair is that there should exist at some time a thing which is the smallest and most insignificant of things, by what the feminine pronoun indicated.

Since it was known [that] the context, why he affirmed the nun in his saying, consequent upon its smallness: ﴿then it will be﴾, is an indication of its stability in its place. And so that the soul's longing for the place of benefit may increase, and the mind may go in every direction, knowing that the aim is great, by omitting the nun and affirming this, he made it difficult after having belittled it, by saying, expressing the greatest concealment and the most complete safeguarding: ﴿in a rock﴾, that is, whatever rock it might be, even if it were the hardest and strongest of rocks, and the smallest and most hidden of them.

When he concealed and narrowed, he revealed and widened, raised and lowered, so that its loss would be greater because of its insignificance, and he said: ﴿or in the heavens﴾, that is, in any place of them, despite the breadth of their expanses and the distance of their regions. He repeated "or" explicitly to indicate the intention of each of them separately, and the preposition as an emphasis of the meaning, and he said: ﴿or in the earth﴾, [that is] likewise. This, as you see, does not preclude that the rock be in both of them or in one of them. He expressed for Him with the greatest Name because of the loftiness of the station, and he said: ﴿Allah will bring it forth﴾, with the greatness of His majesty, the dazzling of His grandeur and perfection, exactly as it is, nothing of it hidden from Him or lost, so that He will call it to account for it. Then he gave the reason for that from His knowledge and power by saying, emphasizing, indicating that denial of that, because of its dazzling greatness, is a habit of souls when they are not accompanied by success: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, and he repeated the greatest Name to alert to the summoning of greatness and to generalize the ruling, ﴿is Subtle﴾, that is, of great reaching through hidden, fine, and obscure matters in attaining a matter He wills, even by means contrary to the path that appears to creation as leading to it, ﴿Aware﴾, of profound knowledge of the most hidden things, so nothing is hidden from Him, and no matter escapes Him.

When He alerted him to the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah, glory be to Him, and to His establishing the reckoning, He commanded him with what he should store up for that, as a means of drawing near to Him and humbling himself before Him. This is the foremost of what sets right the deed and makes tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness) sound and true. So he said: ﴿O my dear son﴾, repeating the address in this manner to indicate the abundance of sincere advice due to the abundance of compassion. ﴿Establish the prayer﴾, i.e., with all its limits and conditions, and do not neglect it, striving for the salvation of your soul and the purification of your inner self. For establishing it, which is performing it in the pleasing manner, prevents deficiency in the deed. ﴿Indeed, prayer forbids immorality and wrongdoing﴾ (Al-'Ankabut: 45), because it is turning toward the One whom you have affirmed as one, believing that He alone is the doer, and turning away from all else, since in reality everything else is nonexistence. For this turning and turning away, it was the second [pillar] of tawhid. He omitted mention of zakat, to indicate that among His wisdom is that He divests him and his son of the world, even of what would suffice them for their sustenance.

When he commanded him to perfect himself, fulfilling the right of the Truth, he followed that with perfecting himself by perfecting others, fulfilling the right of creation. That is because people in this abode are travelers, and the traveler, if he neglects his companion until the companion is seized, is about to be seized himself. So [Luqman] commanded him with what completes his salvation by completing his companion's. He put it first, though it belongs to the acquisition of benefits, because it entails abandoning wrongdoing, whereas abandoning wrongdoing does not entail doing good. For if you say, "Do not commit an abomination," in common usage that covers nothing but refraining from committing sin, not performing obedience. So he said: ﴿And enjoin what is right﴾, i.e., everyone you are able to enjoin, refining others out of compassion for yourself, by rescuing the sons of your kind.

When this abode was a ship for the voyage of those in it to their Lord, and sins were corrupting it, and the corruption of the ship drowns everyone in it (both the one who corrupted it and the one who neglected the corrupter and did not seize his hand), and enjoining right is forbidding wrong, he made this explicit, saying: ﴿And forbid﴾, i.e., everyone you are able to forbid, ﴿wrongdoing﴾, out of love for your brother what you love for yourself, realizing your sincere advice and completing your worship. For no one worships Allah while leaving another to worship other than Him. Of this kind is the saying of Abu al-Aswad, may Allah have mercy on him:

Begin with yourself and restrain it from its errancy,
So when it desists from it, you are wise.

Because He first commanded him with what is right, which is the prayer that forbids immorality and wrongdoing, it is fitting that when he commands and forbids himself, he commands and forbids others. Although this is from the saying of Luqman, peace be upon him, since it was in the context of praising him, we are addressed by it.

Since the one who holds fast to his religion in most times is like one who grasps a live coal, for he opposes the majority, and they shoot at him from a single bow, especially if he commands them and forbids them, He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And be patient﴾ with a great patience, such that it is elevated ﴿over what﴾, i.e., that which, and He confirmed with the past tense that there must be an affliction, so that the person be possessed of insight. So He said: ﴿befalls you﴾, i.e., in your worship, from enjoining right and other things, whether it came through people or not, like illness and the like. He began this injunction with prayer and ended it with patience, because prayer is the foundation of seeking help: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer﴾ (Al-Baqarah: 45). The difference in the addressee in the two places required the difference in the two orders: the addressee here is a believer of few worldly means, and there a disbeliever of abundant means.

Since what he has decreed for him is of great benefit, and He made its conclusion patience, which is the foundation of all deeds and abandonments, He alerted him to that by saying, as an explanation and as a new sentence, signaling exaltation: ﴿Indeed, that﴾, i.e., the great matter I have enjoined upon you, especially patience over calamities, ﴿is of the determined matters of affairs﴾, i.e., their resolved things, using the verbal noun in place of the passive or active participle. That is, matters that are definitively settled, obligatory, or decisive through the firm resolve of their doer; matters worthy that the resolute one set his resolve upon them, and that the firm one incline toward them with his whole self. So there is no escape from abandoning them in any way, in any religion among the religions.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 31, verse 18:

Since among the afflictions of worship, especially commanding and forbidding (because they are imagined in the form of superiority), is self-admiration that leads to arrogance, he said, warning against that and expressing arrogance by its concomitant, because negating the more general thing is negating the more specific, alerting that what is required in commanding and forbidding is gentleness, not the harshness and roughness that bring about aversion: ﴿And do not turn your cheek away﴾, meaning do not incline it deliberately, deliberately bending the neck to do so, turning away from the intended condition. The root of ṣa'r (ṣa'r) is a disease that afflicts the camel, causing it to twist its neck. Nafi', Abu 'Amr, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read "tuṣā'ir" (تُصاعِرْ). The meaning of the form with mufā'ala and taf'il is the deliberate doing of that for the sake of arrogance until it becomes a habit, and the intended prohibition is against what the one who turns away (al-muṣa'ir) does of arrogance. And Allah knows best.

Since that may be for some purpose among the purposes that are not blameworthy, he indicated the intended meaning by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿to people﴾, with the particle of causation (lam al-ʿillah), meaning: do not do that (p-177) for the sake of turning away from them, and that happens only out of contempt for them stemming from arrogance. Rather, turn toward them with your whole face, cheerful and open, without arrogance or haughtiness. He followed that with what it entails, saying: ﴿And do not walk﴾. Since the style is one of humility and dispraise of arrogance, He reminded him that its origin is dust, and he cannot exceed it, so He said: ﴿in the earth﴾. He placed the verbal noun in the position of a circumstantial phrase or a cause, so He said: ﴿exultantly﴾, meaning with strutting and swaggering, meaning: let this reality not be from you, for that is the walk of insolence, wantonness and pride, and such a person is apt to wrong, to transgress and to rebel. Rather, ﴿walk in modesty﴾, for that leads you to humility, so you reach every good, and the earth will be gentle with you when you become, in reality, one who will lie in its belly.

Since the ultimate aim of that is showing off to people and boasting over them, which produces their hatred born of the hatred of Allah, Exalted is He, He gave the reason for it by saying, emphasizing because many people suppose that the abundance of worldly blessings is a sign of Allah's love: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, meaning the One for whom alone arrogance is fitting because of His absolute greatness. And since the love of Allah, which entails the love of people, is beloved to souls, and the loss of what is beloved is harder on souls than the occurrence of what is feared, and since "lā" enters only upon the imperfect (present/future) verb, He said: ﴿does not love﴾, meaning in what is yet to come in time; had He said "yubghidu" (hates), it would admit of restriction to the present state. And since the disordered arrangement is more eloquent because of the closeness of return in a descending manner, within what ascends in the one who comes forward, He said: ﴿every arrogant﴾, meaning one who shows off to people in his walk, strutting, seeing for himself superiority over people and so lifting his nose high; and that is the act of the exultant one, ﴿boastful﴾, who enumerates his virtues; and that is the act of the one who turns away, because that is of the arrogance with which He, glorified and exalted, is clothed; whoever contends with Him for it, He breaks him.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on surah 31, verse 19:

Since the prohibition of that (i.e., of arrogance and insolence) is a command to its opposites, and since the command to moderate one's bearing (*iṭlāq al-wajh*) necessarily entails fairness in speech, and since fairness in speech and walking that is not in the manner of exultance and boasting may prompt one to exert oneself excessively in walking and speaking, or to hasten in walking, or to raise the voice in private and in public beyond the limit, he said, guarding in the command to noble character against what approaches base conduct: ﴿And be moderate﴾, that is, be just and take the middle course, ﴿in your walking﴾, neither excessive nor deficient, keeping aloof from the leaping of the rogues and the dragging gait of those who feign lifelessness. On the authority of Ibn Mas'ud: "They were forbidden from the trotting of the Jews and the creeping of the Christians." Moderation in actions is like justice in weights. Al-Razi said in *al-Lawami'* that it is the gentle walk in which there is no affectation before people, neither with humility nor with arrogance. ﴿And lower﴾, that is, reduce, ﴿from your voice﴾, with the particle "min" affirmed, meaning, so that your voice is not objectionable, and so that raising the voice beyond the need does not make you a donkey. As for when there is need, as in the call to prayer (*adhān*), it is commanded.

Since raising the voice beyond the customary level is objectionable, just as lowering it below that level is feigned lifelessness or affectation and arrogance, and since he had indicated the prohibition of this by "min," it is understood that both extremes are blameworthy. He gave the reason for the prohibition regarding the first (raising the voice), indicating through the form *afʿal* (the comparative) that the whole of raising the voice shares in the objectionableness, mentioning its worst degree, depicting it in the ugliest form to repel one from it. He said: ﴿Indeed, the most hateful of voices﴾, that is, the most atrocious, most hideous and most repellent [all of them], which share in the objectionableness through raising them above the need. He left the speech free of the word of comparison and placed it in the mode of metaphor, depicting the voice of one who raises his voice beyond the need in the form of braying, and making the one who raises his voice as such a donkey, as an exaggeration in disparagement and as an alert that it is among the things God dislikes. So he said: ﴿is the voice of donkeys﴾, that is, this genus, because of the excessive intensity without need. Its beginning is a groan (*zafīr*) and its end is a sob (*shahīq*), and these two are the actions of the people of the Fire. He used the singular to make it explicit that the genus is intended, lest it be thought that gathering is a condition in this. Mentioning the donkey along with this carries a rhetorical force of blame and insult that nothing else carries, and therefore naming it explicitly is considered vulgar. This indicates that raising the voice with need is not blameworthy, for it is neither objectionable nor repellent.

These verses have called to the noblest of morals, which are the mothers of the three virtues: wisdom, chastity and courage. They commanded justice in them, which is the function of distribution (*taqsīṭ*), which is the mean (*wasaṭ*), which is the gathering-place of the virtues. They forbade the bad morals, which are the extremes that are the origin of vices, arising from excess and deficiency. Thus establishing the prayer, which is the spirit of worship founded on knowledge, is the secret of wisdom and of prohibition. He commanded courage and forbade cowardice. In the prohibition of turning the cheek (*taṣʿīr*) and what accompanies it there is a prohibition of recklessness (*tahawwur*). Moderation in walking and [lowering] in the voice is a command to chastity and a prohibition of self-destructive zeal, stiffness, licentiousness and immorality. In the prohibition of self-destructive zeal there is a prohibition of what may necessarily accompany it of cunning (*jarīza*), which is thinking with deceit that leads to damnation, and of descending into foolishness and heedlessness. What completes the explanation of this is what Shaykh Sa'd al-Din al-Taftazani said in his discussion of consensus (*ijmāʿ*) in his *Talwīḥ*. He said: Indeed the Creator, exalted and sanctified, has composed three powers in the human being. The first is the source of the perception of realities, the longing to reflect on consequences, and the distinguishing between benefits and harms; it is expressed as the rational, intellectual power, and the tranquil, angelic soul. The second is the source of attracting benefits and seeking pleasures from foods, drinks and other things; it is called the appetitive power, the bestial power, and the commanding soul. The third is the source of advancing toward terrors and the longing for domination and elevation; it is the irascible power, the predatory power, and the blaming soul. From the moderation of the first movement arises wisdom, from the second chastity, and from the third courage. The mothers of the virtues are these three, and whatever is other than that is only from their branches and combinations. Each of them is surrounded by two extremes in excess and deficiency, which are two vices. As for wisdom, it is knowing realities as they are, to the extent of capacity; it is beneficial knowledge, expressed as knowing the soul's what is for it and what is against it, referred to by the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And whoever is given wisdom has certainly been given much good﴾ [al-Baqarah: 269]. Its excess is *jarbaza*, which is using thought in what should not be used, such as the ambiguous matters, and in a manner that is not fitting, such as opposing the sacred laws — we seek refuge in God from knowledge that does not benefit. I say: it is with a *jīm*, then a *rāʾ* (unpointed), then a *bāʾ*, then a *zāy*, derived from *al-jarbaz*, with a *ḍamma*, which is trickery, that is, wicked deception. And God knows best. Its deficiency is dullness, which is the suspension of the power of thought by the will and abstaining from acquiring beneficial sciences. As for courage, it is the submission of the predatory power to the rational faculty, so that its advance is according to deliberation without agitation in the matters that present themselves, until its action is beautiful and its patience praiseworthy. Its excess is recklessness (*tahawwur*), that is, advancing into what should not be advanced into, and its deficiency is cowardice, that is, caution about what should not be feared. As for chastity, it is the submission [of] the bestial to the rational, so that its conduct is according to what the rational faculty requires, in order to be safe from the subjugation of desire over it and from making pleasures its servants. Its excess is licentiousness and immorality, that is, falling into increasing pleasures beyond what is required. Its deficiency is stiffness (*jumūd*), that is, abstaining from seeking pleasure to the degree that reason and the sacred law have permitted, out of preference rather than by natural constitution. So the means are virtues, and the extremes are vices. When the three virtues are mixed, there results from their union a similar state, which is justice (*ʿadāla*). On this basis, justice is expressed by moderation (*wasāṭa*), that is, in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And thus We made you a justly balanced nation﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143], and to this is pointed the saying of the one upon whom be blessings and peace: "The best of matters are their middle." The wisdom in the bestial soul is the survival of the body, which is the composite of the rational soul, so that it may reach its fitting perfection and its intended goal toward which it is directed. In the predatory power is the breaking and subduing of the bestial, and the repelling of the corruption expected from its domination. He required moderation in their actions, lest the rational faculty be enslaved by their desires and they divert it from its perfection and goal. End.

When these sentences were complete, raising their necks above Jupiter (al-Mushtari) and Saturn (Zuhal), receptive to whoever wishes to act upon them despite laziness, weariness in reflection and boredom, and how far the Pleiades (al-Thurayya) are from the hand of one who reaches for them. He, glory be to Him and exalted, had informed at the beginning of the surah that the verses that are heard are guidance for some people and misguidance for others. It is one of the wonders that a single thing affects two opposites. He followed this with what indicates that it comes from the utmost wisdom, through pleasing, radiant and luminous aspects, yet through subtle paths and hidden allusions. He concluded with the prohibition of arrogance and of raising the voice beyond need, as an indication that the one who does what is not needed is not wise. Arrogance toward people and looking down on them are among the effects of excess in blessing. It was the custom that sovereignty is submitted to at times for mere greatness, at times out of fear of its might, and at times in hope of its favour. He, glory be to Him and exalted, manifested the unseen aspect of what He described the heard verses with, namely the effect of two opposites in one state, within the visible verses, in a manner that indicates His deserving of worship, in accordance with what Luqman, peace be upon him, commanded regarding worship and humility, and that to Him is the return. He is knowing of everything, powerful over everything, and that everything you see was created by Him, reminding that blessing is only from Him. So no one should boast of what another has given him, and if he were left to himself he would not be able to do anything of it. He warns against withdrawing it from the arrogant and giving it to the humble and despised. (p-184) He said: ﴿Have you not seen﴾, that is, know with a knowledge that in its clarity is like direct witnessing, O you who purchase idle talk, you who are arrogant toward Me and who turn away from God, who withdraw from the world, to whom We said, repelling them from shirk and distancing them from desire and falsehood: ﴿This is the creation of God; show Me then what those other than Him have created﴾ [Luqman: 11]. ﴿That God﴾, that is, the One possessing every perfection, ﴿has subjected to you﴾, that is, specifically for you, ﴿whatever is in the heavens﴾, through illumination and darkness, heat and cold, and other favours. He emphasised it by repeating the relative pronoun and the preposition, because the context deserves that. He said: ﴿and whatever is in the earth﴾, with everything that benefits you, so that you know that all of it is His creation, and none of those other than Him has any share in it, and that He encompasses everything in power and knowledge. So He is capable of making it subservient to you, and He will inform you of what you used to do, and bring it to you even if it is in the most hidden places. ﴿And He has lavished﴾, that is, He prolonged, widened, completed and bestowed beyond the measure of need, and perfected, ﴿upon you﴾, O responsible ones, ﴿His blessings﴾ (p-185) [i.e.] one blessing suitable to this world, according to the reading of the majority with a sukun on the ʿayn and a feminine ta' in the accusative, with tanwin of magnification, indicating that it has very many kinds, as indicated by the reading of the Madinans, Abu ʿAmr and Hafs from ʿAsim, which makes the feminine ta' a pronoun referring to Him, glory be to Him, with a fatha on the ʿayn so that it is plural: ﴿apparent﴾, which is what you witness and remember, ﴿and hidden﴾, which is what is absent from you so that they do not perceive it; or you perceive it while it is hidden from you, and you do not mention it except when reminded, and each of you knows this in general. So worship Him by what the counsel of Luqman, peace be upon him, calls to, that you may be among the good-doers, out of caution against the withdrawal of His blessings and the incurring of His punishments. It is permissible that the verse be evidence for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He created the heavens without pillars that you see﴾ [Luqman: 10].

Since the intended sense is: and while each of you, O creatures, knows that this is a blessing from Him alone, glory be to Him and exalted, some people submit, turn in repentance, and surrender to all that His Wise Book calls to through the tongue of His noble Prophet, and so they are among the wise and the good-doers, and are guided. He followed it by His saying, manifesting the place of the [pronoun of the] addressees in what the wording of the unbelievers alludes to: ﴿And among people﴾, that is, those who are fit for disturbance. It is possible that it is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) of ﴿Have you not seen﴾, and ﴿Have you not seen﴾ (p-186) is evidence for the beginning of the surah, meaning: the verses are pointed to while being guidance for whoever is mentioned, and the state is that among people is one who purchases idle talk. ﴿Have you not seen﴾ is evidence that among people is the obstinate one after the clarity of the proof, that God has subjected to you the whole world and bestowed upon you what He has bestowed, while among people is ﴿one who disputes﴾; there is no idle talk greater than his disputing, no arrogance like his arrogance, and no misguidance like his misguidance. He made it apparent to add reproach to this disputant, and as an indication of the ugliness of disputing without regard to the blessings. So He said, exalted is He: ﴿concerning God﴾, the One who encompasses everything in knowledge and power.

Since He, glory be to Him, is in the manifestation of His existence and attributes to such a degree that He is not hidden in any way, and since the disputant may be intelligent, He said: ﴿without﴾, that is, with speech characterised as being not ﴿knowledge﴾, that is, rather with words whose meanings are feeble, because they are not grounded in sense or reason, joined to the sounds of dumb animals. Thus by that he is a donkey following his desire.

Since the meaning may appear to some of the lesser minds, because it comes from the tongue of one who is not regarded, if it is attributed to a great person it is pondered and one does not hasten to reject it out of respect for it, so it appears through the length of its sensation. He said, expressing with the particle of negation that is proper to it, because the place calls for it, and he departed from it first lest it be thought that what is blamed is only the disputant when he is not characterised by knowledge (p-187) [even if his disputing is characterised by knowledge]: ﴿nor guidance﴾, that is, coming from one known to be sound in words and deeds through the miracles and clear signs he has shown; so it is obligatory to accept his sayings as submitted to, even if their meaning does not appear.
